prompt:
Synthetic museum-administration exercise. An invented museum network has a conservation-review policy for loans. Explain which proposed loans require review and which facts remain unresolved. The curator has received a standard policy, a signed exception, an internal summary, and incomplete project records. This packet is a fictional closed rule system and is not advice about real contracts or cultural-property law.

[B20-S1: network policy effective March 1] A physical loan from a network museum to an outside institution requires conservation review if its insured value exceeds 50,000 units. Related physical loans for the same exhibition project, departing within any thirty-day interval, are aggregated before applying that threshold. “Related” means organized under the same exhibition agreement, not merely made by the same borrower. Digital image licenses are outside this physical-loan policy and are not added to insured loan value. Loans entirely between network museums are exempt from this review threshold. The policy does not abolish other approvals, and this packet supplies no rules for those other approvals.

[B20-S2: signed exception and delegation] An authorized network director signed an exception on April 10 for the named exhibition River Rooms. It permits that exhibition's physical loans to depart without threshold review until April 30 inclusive, provided every item is accompanied by an approved condition report. The exception does not waive the condition-report requirement and does not name any other exhibition. A delegation schedule allows local curators to certify condition reports but does not authorize them to extend director-signed exceptions. An email from a local curator says, “I am happy to keep this arrangement going into May.” No director approval of an extension appears in the packet.

[B20-S3: proposed transactions] Loan Ash, insured for 30,000, departs April 20 from a network museum to outside institution Harbor Hall under the River Rooms agreement; its condition report is approved. Loan Beech, insured for 25,000, departs April 28 to Harbor Hall under the same agreement, but its condition report is still awaiting certification. Loan Elm, insured for 35,000, departs May 5 to Harbor Hall. Its booking record uses project code RR-2, but the underlying exhibition agreement is missing; the packet does not establish whether RR-2 is part of River Rooms or a separate project. A digital-image license worth 20,000 is issued to Harbor Hall on April 21. Loan Fir, insured for 90,000, departs April 22 between two network museums.

[B20-S4: summaries and questions] An internal checklist says “all Harbor Hall loans are covered by the April exception” and tells staff to add image-license fees to insured values. Its author did not consult the signed exception. A planning note says Beech should be considered approved because certification is routine, but the certifier has not examined its condition report. A publicity sheet praises the exhibition's historical importance. Harbor Hall asks whether splitting a shipment over several dates avoids the threshold, while a registrar asks whether Elm's later departure invalidates the earlier loans retroactively.

Explain the threshold calculation and the exception's independent conditions. Distinguish borrower identity from exhibition identity, permission to certify from authority to extend, and a proposed or expected approval from an approval actually recorded. Give conditional conclusions for the missing Elm agreement without inventing it. Explain why an exception valid for qualifying departures in April is not automatically erased by a later May transaction, while the May transaction must be assessed under the applicable rule and aggregation window. Stay within conservation review rather than claiming every loan is fully authorized for all purposes.
response:
**Ash qualifies for the April exception; Beech's exemption depends on its still-unapproved condition report; Elm's review requirement depends on its missing exhibition agreement.** The digital license is outside this policy, and Fir is exempt from this threshold because it stays within the network. These conclusions concern conservation review, not every approval a transaction might need. [B20-S1–S3]

### Apply aggregation before the exception

The ordinary rule requires review when related outside physical loans departing within any thirty-day interval have a combined insured value **exceeding 50,000 units**. “Related” means under the same exhibition agreement. Sharing Harbor Hall as borrower is insufficient. Digital-license fees are not part of the calculation. [B20-S1]

Ash and Beech share the River Rooms agreement and depart eight days apart, so their combined insured value is:

\[
30{,}000+25{,}000=55{,}000\text{ units}.
\]

That exceeds the threshold even though each loan individually falls below it. Splitting these departures across dates therefore does not avoid review under the ordinary rule. A calendar-month boundary also does not reset the thirty-day window. [B20-S1; B20-S3]

The signed exception then permits qualifying River Rooms departures through April 30 inclusive to proceed without threshold review, provided every departing item has an approved condition report. Exhibition identity, departure date, and approved reports are separate conditions; satisfying one does not satisfy the others. [B20-S2]

| Transaction | Conservation-review conclusion on the supplied facts |
| --- | --- |
| Ash: April 20, 30,000 units | Meets the recorded April-exception conditions, so threshold review is waived. |
| Beech: April 28, 25,000 units | Ordinary aggregation triggers review. It can qualify for the April exception if its condition report is approved before departure. That approval is currently pending. |
| Elm: May 5, 35,000 units | Outside the recorded exception period; aggregation depends on its exhibition agreement. |
| Digital license: April 21, 20,000 units | Outside this physical-loan policy and excluded from insured-value totals. |
| Fir: April 22, 90,000 units | Exempt from this threshold because both museums are in the network. |

The transaction details and report statuses are from [B20-S3]; the governing rule and exception are [B20-S1; B20-S2]. Routine certification is still a future possibility, not an approval already recorded. Threshold review would not itself certify Beech's report or fulfill the exception's report condition. [B20-S2; B20-S4]

### Elm has two possible outcomes

**If RR-2 belongs to the River Rooms agreement**, Ash, Beech, and Elm all fall within one thirty-day interval, April 20 to May 5. Their combined insured value is **90,000 units**. Elm consequently requires threshold review: it exceeds the aggregated threshold and departs after the exception expires. The April waiver does not remove the earlier related loans' values from the aggregation rule. [B20-S1–S3]

**If RR-2 is a separate exhibition agreement**, the listed loans do not aggregate with Elm merely because Harbor Hall borrows them all. Elm's known project total is then **35,000 units**, so these records do not trigger threshold review for Elm. The missing agreement is the evidence needed to choose between these outcomes; the project code alone cannot settle it. [B20-S1; B20-S3]

### Authority and timing matter

Local curators may certify reports, but they may not extend director-signed exceptions. The curator's email therefore does not establish a May extension. No director-approved extension is documented in the packet; that is a limit of the record, not proof that no such approval could exist elsewhere. [B20-S2]

Elm's May departure does not retroactively cancel a valid exception for qualifying April departures. Ash remains covered on its recorded facts; Beech's April coverage still depends on actual certification. Elm must separately satisfy the May rule, including aggregation with related April departures where applicable. [B20-S1–S3]

The internal checklist cannot broaden the signed exception or add digital fees to insured values. The exhibition's historical importance also supplies no exemption under the stated rules. Other approvals remain outside what this packet can determine. [B20-S1; B20-S2; B20-S4]
